candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — quality improvement and cost-effective care/resource management, detailed content pp. 19-23.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — quality-linked reimbursement/value-based care
candidate.educational_objective: Distinguish value-based payment from fee-for-service by recognizing that value-based programs link financial incentives to quality and performance rather than service volume alone.

options.A: Payment is increasingly tied to the number of billable services delivered while quality and patient outcomes play a smaller role in financial incentives.
options.B: Payment increasingly rewards quality of care and performance rather than service volume alone, aligning incentives with better care.
options.C: Payment removes formal quality measurement from reimbursement decisions, allowing organizations to focus primarily on increasing procedural volume.
options.D: Payment separates reimbursement from patient outcomes and care quality because value-based models are designed only to simplify billing administration.

candidate.rationale: CMS states that value-based programs reward providers with incentive payments for the quality of care they provide and are intended to move payment toward quality rather than quantity of services. B directly reflects that shift. A describes the volume emphasis value-based programs are intended to move away from, while C and D incorrectly remove quality and performance from payment decisions.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Value-based programs reward providers with incentive payments for quality and move payment toward quality rather than quantity of care; quality performance is linked to payment.
candidate.source_locator: What are the value-based programs?; Why are value-based programs important?; original value-based programs section linking quality performance to payment.
candidate.stem: A health system shifts from fee-for-service toward value-based payment. Which statement best describes the intended change?
